Formula: First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
Exact Expression: G / \ker(\phi) \cong \mathrm{im}(\phi)
Definitions: Fundamental theorem stating that the quotient group of a group by the kernel of a homomorphism is naturally isomorphic to its image.
Derivation/Reference: Derived by Camille Jordan (1870) and formalized by Emmy Noether (1927)
Example: phi: (Z, +) -> ({1, -1}, *) with phi(n) = (-1)^n -> ker(phi) = 2Z -> Z / 2Z cong {1, -1}
Domain: abstract_algebra
Assumptions: phi is a valid group homomorphism
Common Errors: Forgetting that ker(phi) must be a normal subgroup in non-abelian groups
subject: First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
